results.title: 'The Pitt' Wins Emmy For Outstanding Drama Series
results.author: Dade Hayes
results.text:
'The Pitt' Wins Emmy For Outstanding Drama Series

Skip to main content

September 14, 2025 8:44pm

Medical procedural The Pitt captured the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series on Sunday, outdoing fellow category front-runner Severance.

The HBO/ HBO Max rookie’s series trophy followed a Lead Actor win for star Noah Wyle, on his seventh career nomination, and an earlier one by Katherine LaNasa for Supporting Actress.

“This is insane,” said R. Scott Gemmill, creator, executive producer and showrunner, as he stepped to the microphone. After shouting out a number of names, including Warner Bros. Television Group and U.S. Networks chief “Channing [Dungey] for believing in this show from the get-go,” he closed with a big non-industry tribute. “I want to dedicate this on behalf of everyone to all the health care workers, front-line, first responders,” he said. “Respect them, protect them, trust them, thank you!”

### Related Stories

### ‘The Pitt’ Takes Drama Series & ‘The Studio’ Tops Comedy As ‘Adolescence’ Leads The Field – Full Winners List

### Emmy Awards 2025 Photos: Best Of The Red Carpet

The Pitt is somewhat unorthodox among hit originals on streaming or premium cable as a hospital drama with many quintessential traits of a broadcast television series. That resemblance is not accidental, but the degree to which it emulates Hall of Fame medical procedural ER is now a matter of legal dispute. A lawsuit filed by the widow of ER creator and bestselling author Michael Crichton against Warner Bros. Discovery alleges that The Pitt is actually a spinoff of the long-ago NBC mainstay, but participants in the original series have been cut out of the proceeds.

The fact that Wyle, a longtime ER cast member, is the lead of The Pitt has only deepened the intrigue. In his acceptance speech Sunday, Wyle thanked Warner Bros. Television for “allowing the conditions to exist for lightning to strike twice in my life.”

Despite the legal shadow cast over the show, viewers certainly haven’t been dissuaded by it. The Pitt has been a reliable performer for HBO Max, averaging more than 10 million viewers per episode, according to WBD. Even before the premiere of Season 1 in January 2025, HBO execs said they were looking at other procedurals to possibly follow the series onto the air and on HBO Max.

results.author: Jesse Pasternack
results.text:
Adulation for Adolescence, The Studio Sets New Record for Comedy Series at 77th Emmy Awards | Television Academy

 Awards News September 15, 2025 

Adulation for Adolescence, The Studio Sets New Record for Comedy Series at 77th Emmy Awards

The Pitt takes Outstanding Drama, The Traitors repeats as Outstanding Reality Competition Series.

 By Jesse Pasternack 

Netflix’s Adolescence surpassed its older peers by winning six awards at the 77th Emmys, the most for a single program on the night, including Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series. Apple TV+’s The Studio followed with four wins, including Outstanding Comedy Series. HBO Max’s freshman medical drama The Pitt was next with three Emmys, including Outstanding Drama Series.

Peacock’s The Traitors won its second consecutive Emmy for Outstanding Reality Competition Program and swept all five categories in which it was nominated this year, one tonight and four at last week’s Creative Arts ceremonies. HBO’s Last Week Tonight received the Emmy for Outstanding Scripted Variety Series for the third consecutive year and Outstanding Writing for a Variety Series for the eighth consecutive year.

The Studio's Seth Rogen accepts the Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series Photo Credit: Invision/AP

The Studio's Seth Rogen won for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series / Invision/AP

CBS’s The Late Show with Stephen Colbert scored its first-ever Emmy, for Outstanding Talk Series. The well wishes for the beloved late night host, as reflected in the lengthy cheers and chant of “Stephen! Stephen!” for his first win after the July announcement that his show would end next year, were echoed backstage before the winner in his category was called.

Fifty years after winning his first Emmy, Lorne Michaels took home his 22nd Emmy for NBC’s SNL50: The Anniversary Special. 

In addition to its win for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series, Adolescence, a wrenching drama about a teenager accused of murder and the effects of the accusation on the young man and his family, made history. Fifteen-year-old Owen Cooper became the youngest male Emmy acting winner ever by capturing Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for his performance in Netflix’s Adolescence. Erin Doherty grabbed Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie and Stephen Graham won for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie. Graham and Jack Thorne received the prize for Outstanding Writing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie, and Philip Barantini prevailed in the category of Outstanding Directing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie.

The Studio, a frantic farce about the pitfalls of being an executive at a major motion picture studio, broke The Bear’s record of 11, established in 2023, for most Emmys won by a comedy, with 13 — four tonight and nine at last weekend’s Creative Arts ceremonies. In addition to its win for Outstanding Comedy Series, The Studio's other victories included Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for Seth Rogen; Outstanding Directing for a Comedy Series for Rogen and Evan Goldberg; and Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series for Rogen, Goldberg, Peter Huyck, Alex Gregory and Frida Perez.

Adolescence's Stephen Graham and Jack Thorne / Invision/AP

Beyond its win for Outstanding Drama Series, The Pitt, which follows a demanding day in a Pittsburgh emergency room, had two newly minted first-time Emmy winners in Katherine LaNasa for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama and Noah Wyle for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series. 

Apple TV+’s Severance garnered two Emmys. Britt Lower took home Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series and the untrammeled Tramell Tillman victoriously made history as the first Black man to win Best Supporting Actor in a Drama Series.

Other acting honors included two for the HBO Max comedy Hacks. Jean Smart took home her third consecutive Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series Emmy, and Hannah Einbender won her first Emmy for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series.

Another HBO comedy, Somebody Somewhere, received its first Emmy when Jeff Hiller, nominated for the first time, was named Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Comedy. Fellow first-time nominee Cristin Milioti took home Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for HBO’s The Penguin. 

Andor, streaming on Disney+, took its lone Emmy of the night for Dan Gilroy in the category of Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series. Adam Randall scored the Emmy for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series for the Apple TV+ program Slow Horses. 

In addition to the Emmys voted on by the Television Academy membership, a special award, the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award, chosen by the Academy's board of governors, was given to Mary Steenburgen and Ted Danson. Established in 2002, it is given to “an individual(s) in the media industry whose deeds and actions have a lasting impact on communities and whose philanthropic efforts exemplify Bob Hope’s decades-long altruism and positive impact on society.” The couple received the award for their work supporting numerous causes, including ocean preservation and environmentalism; incarcerated and formerly incarcerated citizens; funding for the arts; and for co-founding Angels at Risk, a nonprofit focused on young people who are at risk for drugs and alcohol abuse as well as their families.

The team from The Pitt accepts the award for Outstanding Drama/ Invision/AP

The ceremony — hosted by comedian Nate Bargatze and broadcast live on CBS — took place at the Peacock Theater at LA Live in Downtown Los Angeles.

The Academy's Primetime Awards Committee is led by chair Debra Curtis and co-vice chairs Anya Adams and Jacob Fenton. 

The executive producers of the 77th Emmy Awards — returning for a third time — were Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay of Jesse Collins Entertainment.

A complete list of winners is available here.

# ‘The Pitt’ Wins Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series

The tense series, which unfolds over the course of a single day, brought the medical drama roaring back into the zeitgeist.

### Christian Zilko

More stories by Christian

‘Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!’ Trailer: Rinko Kikuchi Dances Her Way Through Grief in Sundance Hit

‘The Thomas Crown Affair’ Teaser: Michael B. Jordan Directs Himself as Cinema’s Coolest Thief

Tony Gilroy’s ‘Behemoth!’ to World Premiere as New York Film Festival Centerpiece

September 14, 2025 11:01 pm

Noah Wyle in 'The Pitt'

Courtesy of Warrick Page / Max

Share

Show more sharing options

“ The Pitt” has appeared to be unstoppable from the moment it debuted on HBO Max, picking up fans at an overwhelming pace with its tense storytelling and breathing new life into the medical drama genre. That momentum continued all the way through the 77th Primetime Emmy Awards, as the show has won the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series in its first season.

The award marked the end of a huge night for the rookie drama, which ended up winning five Emmy’s including Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for Noah Wyle and Supporting Actress in a Drama Series for Katherine LaNasa. The show had previously won Emmy’s for Casting and Guest Actor in a Drama Series for Shawn Hatosy, which were announced at last weekend’s Creative Arts Emmy Awards.

Related Stories

Nick Antosca Made ‘Cape Fear’ His Own with Scorsese and Spielberg’s Blessing — and Their Notes

‘Fightland’ Review: 50 Cent’s Starz Boxing Drama Is All Hype and No Hooks

Created by R. Scott Gemmill and executive produced by medical drama veteran John Wells, the show follows the doctors and nurses at an underfunded Pittsburgh emergency room over the course of a single, fateful, day. Each episode covers one hour of the day, allowing viewers to feel the urgency of medical professionals working in real time as they juggle multiple patients.

As TV creators have continued to innovate and blur the boundaries with film in recent years, traditional genres like medical dramas have not exactly been trendy. But “The Pitt” proved that, when executed at the highest level, the timeless genre can produce some of the best television you’ll ever watch. Speaking to IndieWire at the time of the show’s premiere, Wells explained that part of the show’s appeal stems from its ability to shine a spotlight on the labor of humans who are doing their best to make the world a better place.

“The fact that we’re showing just how difficult the emergency room situation is in the country means that people go, ‘Oh, that’s true. That’s the experience that happened for me and that I see some people who are actually trying to make a difference,’” Wells said. “They’re there. They can be doing any number of other things. All these physicians could be making two and three times more by trying to do a different specialty. And they’re actually there to care for the people who need it, usually in the most dire circumstances, or you simply have no other health care.”

“The Pitt” received 12 Primetime Emmy nominations for its first season. The show was quickly renewed for Season 2, which is scheduled to premiere in January 2026. Watch the first teaser for the new season here.

results.author: Larisha Paul
results.text:
'The Pitt' Wins Outstanding Drama Series at 2025 Emmy Awards

×

Skip to main content

The Pitt accepts the award for Outstanding Drama at the 2025 Emmy Awards VALERIE MACON/AFP/Getty Images

ER, the medical drama that brought Noah Wyle together with writer R. Scott Gemmill and executive producer John Wells, earned 23 Emmy Awards over the course of its 15-season run. Earlier this year, the trio returned with The Pitt, another hospital-based drama that adopts an unconventional, hour-by-hour approach to the traditional format. And on Sunday night, the show began to build its own Emmys collection, including a win for Outstanding Drama Series.

After taking the stage, Gemmill used his brief acceptance speech to thank real-life healthcare workers for inspiring the show. “I want to dedicate this on behalf of everyone to all the healthcare workers, frontline first-responders,” said Gemmill. “Respect them. Protect them. Trust them.”

the pitt wins the emmy for best drama series!!!!!!!! pic.twitter.com/AFLyV0mmqI

> — Jo 🩵 (@jo_yells) September 15, 2025

The Pitt faced off with a competitive set of nominated series, including Andor, The Diplomat, The Last of Us, Paradise, Severance, Slow Horses, and The White Lotus.

Just earlier in the evening, Noah Wyle won the award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for his role as Dr. Robby, and Katherine LaNasa won for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series for her role as Nurse Dana Evans.

The HBO Max series scored additional nominations in Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series for Amanda Marsalis and John Wells, and Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series for R. Scott Gemmill and Joe Sachs.

Each episode of the series centers on a specific hour in the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center emergency room. The Pitt returns for another shift in January, picking up during the July 4 weekend, around 10 months after the events of Season One conclude.

“That’s what the audience comes for: to be surprised, and challenged,” Gemmill told Rolling Stone earlier this year. “The compression in one day is a conceit, but I think it worked. What was really amazing is how quickly the cast and crew adapted to it. The first day was a little crazy… By the end of the first episode, we were just humming along like we’ve been doing it for 10 years. It was really, really impressive how quickly everyone fell into that rhythm.”

- The Pitt won the award for Best Drama Series at the Emmys 2025 and showrunner R. Scott Gemmill dedicated the prize to healthcare workers
- Andor, The Diplomat, The Last of Us, Paradise, Severance, Slow Horses and The White Lotus were also nominated in the category
- The hit series was nominated 13 awards at this year’s awards ceremony

And the most dramatic show of the year is...The Pitt.

The series took home the big prize for Outstanding Drama Series at the 2025 Emmy Awards on Sunday, Sept. 14.

“This is insane. Thank you so much to the Academy,” the series’ creator and showrunner R. Scott Gemmillsaid on stage before thanking the team behind the show at Warner Bros and HBO Max, adding, “We wouldn’t be out here without you guys.”

“I have the best practicing partners and friends in the world,” he added before giving a nod to executive producer John Wells and star Noah Wyle.

“I want to dedicate this on behalf of everyone, to all the healthcare workers, frontline first responders,” he concluded. “Respect them, protect them, trust them. Thank you!”

Andor, The Diplomat, The Last of Us, Paradise, Severance, Slow Horses and The White Lotus were also nominated in the category.

The Pitt was another of the year's biggest hits, and earned a whopping 13 nominations. The medical drama led by Noah Wyle follows Dr. Robby and took place over the course of one shift in the emergency department, where he's joined by Shawn Hatosy, Katherine LaNasa, Taylor Dearden and Fiona Dourif.

R. Scott Gemmill holds the Outstanding Drama Series award for "The Pitt" during the 77th Primetime Emmy Awards at the Peacock Theatre at LA Live in Los Angeles on September 14, 2025.

VALERIE MACON/AFP via Getty

Wyle told PEOPLE he was "overwhelmed" by his own nomination — for Outstanding Actor in a Drama Series — and the overall recognition for the show as someone who's "been around now for 30 years and done a lot of different things."

" I gave up hope that this was going to be something that my career was going to be part of again," he said. "It's really amazing."

From left: Taylor Dearden, Noah Wyle and Shawn Hatosy in 'The Pitt'.

John Johnson/Max

The second and final season of the hit Disney+ Star Wars prequel series Andor concluded in May and earned 14 Emmy nominations this year, totaling 22 over its two-season run.

The prequel series followed Diego Luna's Cassian Andor, who fans first met in Rogue One: A Star Wars Story in 2022, as he was recruited by the Rebel Alliance to become a spy. Adria Arjona starred alongside Luna as Bix Caleen, the love interest to Cassian.

In a post on Instagram, Luna, 45, celebrated the news of the nominations, writing, "Congratulations to the entire #Andor team!!! So proud of these 14 nominations!! Including Outstanding Drama Series!! Qué chingón!!!"

Bix Caleen (Adria Arjona) and Andor (Diego Luna) in season 2 of 'Andor'.

Lucasfilm Ltd

The Diplomat was once again recognized this year for its second season, which saw Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell's Kate and Hal Wyler reckon with the fallout from an attack on their own in the season 1 finale.

Russell was also nominated for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series at this year's show, her second nomination following one in 2023 for season 1.

The Netflix series is one of the actress' "most favorite jobs I've ever worked on," she told Deadline, so the recognition means a lot.

"To be acknowledged for something that is so fun to make is just such a rare bird."

Keri Russell as Kate Wyler, Rufus Sewell as Hal Wyler in 'The Diplomat' season 3.

Liam Daniel/Netflix

Similarly to The Diplomat, the second season of The Last of Us also brought in a heap of nominations for the HBO series. With 16 nominations in total, including nods for Pedro Pascal, Bella Ramsey, Kaitlyn Dever, Catherine O'Hara, Jeffrey Wright and Joe Pantoliano, the series, which is adapted from the bestselling video game of the same name, was among the most-nominated this year.

Season 2 of the hit series brought heartbreak for fans as Pascal's character, Joel, was killed by a vengeful Abby (Dever), which wasn't exactly unexpected, given it takes place in the video game, but was devastating nonetheless — for the actor, too.

"It was just a matter of how and when," he told Entertainment Weekly of his fate, which he knew was coming. " I'm in active denial."

Pedro Pascal and Bella Ramsey in 'The Last of Us'.

Liane Hentscher/HBO

Paradise was one of the year's biggest breakout hits, and scored four nominations for its first season. Stars Sterling K. Brown, James Marsden and Julianne Nicholson were all recognized for their roles as Agent Xavier Collins, Cal Bradford and Sinatra, respectively, in the twisty Hulu thriller.

Days before the awards show, Brown revealed he'd torn his Achilles heel in an Instagram video, but was postponing surgery to make sure he could attend the Emmys.

Given that the "recovery can take a little bit of time," Brown said he's planning surgery for "after the Emmys, so I can motivate myself and go and try to celebrate with my cast and the producers of Paradise, because we got recognized."

Sterling K. Brown (left) and James Marsden in 'Paradise'.

Disney/Ser Baffo

The long-awaited second season of Apple TV+'s Severance premiered in January, close to three years after season 1 concluded.

The return was met with rave reviews as Adam Scott, John Turturro, Zach Cherry and Britt Lower were back inside Lumon after their innies experienced life as their outies in the dramatic season 1 finale.

Season 2 earned an impressive 27 nominations, including nods for Scott, Turturro, Cherry and Lower, along with Tramell Tillman, Gwendoline Christie, Patricia Arquette, Jane Alexander and Merritt Wever.

Adam Scott as Mark, Zach Cherry as Dylan, John Turturro as Irving and Britt Lower Helly in 'Severance'.

Atsushi Nishijima/Apple TV+

Slow Horses, the Gary Oldman-led spy thriller series, was nominated for Outstanding Drama Series for the second time this year, and the actor himself was also nominated for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for his portrayal of M15 boss Jackson Lamb.

Oldman, 67, told the L.A. Times that the show's success — its fifth season premieres this fall and it's already been renewed for season 6 — has reached as far as Buckingham Palace.

"The Queen said to me, ‘Are there any more?’ I’m led to believe that they like Slow Horses," he told the outlet of Queen Camilla.

“I feel so privileged, so bloody lucky that at 67 years old, I’m in a show of this caliber, that people have really actually embraced," he added of the show. "I’m so very, very blessed, and it’s also nice to know that you’re going to be working."

Gary Oldman in 'Slow Horses'.

Apple TV+

The third season of Mike White's cult classic, The White Lotus, earned 23 nominations this year, with a majority of the cast being recognized.

Natasha Rothwell, Carrie Coon, Parker Posey, Aimee Lou Wood, Walton Goggins, Sam Rockwell, Scott Glenn and Jason Isaacs were all nominated in various categories, along with the show itself receiving several nods.

Season 3 of the series followed a family (Posey, Isaacs, Patrick Schwarzenegger, Sam Nivola and Sarah Catherine Hook), a trio of friends (Coon, Leslie Bibb and Michelle Monaghan) and a couple (Wood and Goggins) as they enjoyed a week away at a luxury resort in Thailand.

In previous seasons, the show has walked away with tons of awards and recognition. The series received a season 4 renewal in January 2025, nearly a month before the season 3 premiere.

On Sept. 4, Deadline reported that creator Mike White had "zeroed in" on the season 4 location: France. HBO did not comment when reached by PEOPLE.

Sam Nivola, Sarah Catherine Hook, Patrick Schwarzenegger, Jason Isaacs, Parker Posey, Morgana O'Reilly in 'The White Lotus' season 3.

Fabio Lovino/HBO

Pop the champagne! It's time to find out which of the year's biggest shows walked away winners at the 2025 Emmy Awards.

Netflix's Adolescence won big at the 77th annual ceremony with six awards, including Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited Series or Movie for 15-year-old star Owen Cooper and Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series. HBO's The Pitt also cleaned up in the drama categories, winning Outstanding Drama Series and Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama for ER alum Noah Wyle.

While Apple TV+'s Severance led the stable of nominees with a whopping 27 nominations — the most of any drama or comedy series — it ultimately earned two acting wins for stars Brit Lower and Tramell Tillman, along with its five wins from last weekend's Creative Emmys.

On the comedy side of the equation, Seth Rogen's The Studio dominated the night after racking up 23 nominations and winning awards for Outstanding Comedy Series and Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for Rogen. Along with its Creative Emmys wins, the Apple TV+ comedy received a record-setting 13 wins.

Stephen Colbert received a standing ovation after winning an Emmy for The Late Show With Stephen Colbert — two months after CBS canceled the long-running show.

The Batman-adjacent HBO show The Penguin won only one award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited Series or Movie for Cristin Milioti. The Television Academy must not have enjoyed its stay at The White Lotus this season, as the Thailand-set third season walked away empty-handed on Sunday.

This year's Emmys ceremony — hosted by comedian Nate Bargatze— also included several reunions of stars from Gilmore Girls, Everybody Loves Raymond, and Annie.
